title_english: Bengawan Solo (The Great River of Solo)
secondary_associations: Java | Surakarta | Indonesian national song repertoire
research_notes: Written 1940 in Surakarta by Gesang Martohartono (then 23) about the Solo River, in Indonesian rather than Javanese. Kroncong style with Portuguese-influenced urban folk roots. Became widely known during the Japanese occupation and after independence; also popular in Japan and elsewhere in East/Southeast Asia. Year 1940 is the composition year.

Written and performed by Freddie Aguilar. Recorded 1977 at Cinema Audio; released 1978 (Vicor/Sunshine). Finalist in the inaugural 1978 Metropop Song Festival, Manila. Produced by Celso Llarina, arranged by Doming Amarillo. Year 1978 is the release year.

original_instruments: Electric guitar | Electric bass | Keyboard | Suling | Gendang
research_notes: Title song of Soneta's first album, sung by Oma Irama, later called Rhoma Irama, with Elvy Sukaesih also on the album. English Wikipedia dates the album to 1973 and describes the band sound as keyboard, two electric guitars, electric bass, suling and gendang. Indonesian Wikipedia dates the release to 1975 and the recording to 1974 at Yukawi Studio, Jakarta, and lists Begadang as track 1 by Oma Irama. A songwriter credit for this track was not on either page, so attribution is Unknown and the year is left empty. A 1978 film of the same name came later.

title_english: Diem xua (Diễm of Those Old Days)
research_notes: Song by Trịnh Công Sơn, sung by Khánh Ly on the tape Sơn Ca 7. The song page and the composer's site date the writing to 1960. His biography page says he wrote it in 1961 out of the attachment to Ngô Vũ Bích Diễm. A works list names an earlier disc by Thái Thanh in 1963 and does not give a composition year. Year is left empty because of that conflict. Khánh Ly sang a Japanese version, Utsukushii mukashi, at the 1970 Osaka fair. Not written as a film theme; NHK later used it. Genre name Vietnamese popular song is outside the older taxonomy list.

songwriter: ស៊ីន ស៊ីសាមុត
research_notes: Ballad by Sinn Sisamouth. The song page and his biography say it was released in 1962 on Wat Phnom Disques, and that a 1971 interview called it the first item aired at the 1966 opening of Royal Khmer Television. A collector's scan of Wat Phnom 45-5044 labels the A-side bolero-twist, music and words by Sinn Sisamouth, orchestra leader Mer Bun. Mānoa (2021) also dates the release to 1962. The catalogue number is from the collector page, not from the encyclopedia, so the status stays partial.

title_original: น้ำตาลาวเวียง
title_english: Namta Lao Wiang (Tears of a Lao Girl of Wiang)
artist: สุรพล สมบัติเจริญ
research_notes: Early luk thung song of Suraphol Sombatcharoen, born Lamduan Sombatcharoen in Suphan Buri. English Wikipedia calls Nam Ta Lao Wieng his first hit, in 1954, and the point at which luk thung emerged. Thai Wikipedia says the first song he recorded was น้ำตาลาวเวียง in 2496 BE (1953). A composer was not named on either page. Year is left empty. He was shot dead on 16 August 1968 after a show in Nakhon Pathom.

title_english: Rayuan Pulau Kelapa (Solace of the Coconut Island)
research_notes: Patriotic song by Ismail Marzuki. His English biography dates it to 1944. ANTARA News describes a signed score in the Taman Ismail Marzuki collection dated 15 November 1944. A 2025 conference paper says he wrote it in October 1944, during the Japanese occupation, and that Rose Kusumabrata sang it at the 1947 World Youth Festival. The day is not entered because October and 15 November disagree. Not written as a film theme. Later used as a TVRI closedown under Suharto.

title_original: အဝေးကချစ်သူ
research_notes: One of five Shan songs Sai Htee Saing wrote and recorded for the Shan service of Burma Broadcasting Service, named on his Burmese biography together with လှေငယ်ရှင်ဆုတောင်း, အကျည်းတန်ချစ်သူ, ကိုယ်သဘောကျသူလေး and ပန်းချယ်ရီ. The English biography says that career began in 1969 with a Shan-language song on that service, and that he was born Sai Tin U on 23 September 1950 in Langkho. The English page does not name this title, so the link between this song and 1969 is inferred from the two accounts of the same first session. Shan popular song was added to the genre list.
